title: Five Paint-Prep Mistakes That Make a Simple Room Look Unfinished
description: The boring preparation steps that usually matter more than buying a more expensive paint colour.
body_html:
A good paint job is mostly decided before the first coat goes on. Rushing preparation often creates visible edges, uneven coverage and repairs that take longer than the prep would have.

1. Painting over dust

Dust and loose debris can keep paint from bonding cleanly. Clean the surface using a method appropriate for the wall and existing finish, then let it dry before painting.

2. Ignoring damaged surfaces

Paint does not hide every dent or crack. Fill suitable imperfections, allow the repair to dry and sand it smooth. For recurring cracks or signs of moisture, find the underlying cause first.

3. Skipping a test patch

Colour and sheen can look different under your actual room lighting. Test a small area and view it during the times of day when you normally use the room.

4. Forgetting edges and protection

Protect floors and surfaces before opening the paint. Remove or protect hardware where practical. Clean, deliberate edges are easier when the workspace is not fighting you.

5. Applying another coat too soon

Follow the paint manufacturer's drying and recoating guidance. A surface that feels dry is not necessarily ready for the next step.

Before you paint

  • Clean and dry the surface.
  • Repair visible damage.
  • Test the colour.
  • Protect floors and hardware.
  • Check the product instructions.

Preparation feels slow because it is not very photogenic. It is also one of the cheapest ways to improve the final result.
